items.title: Adaptive conditional-kernel hybrid telescope

source.anchor: Section 6.1, Lemma 6.3 and its adjacent-hybrid proof
source.attribution: The adaptive sampler and Lemma 6.3 are due to Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. The explicit measurable-kernel decomposition is ASTIS's rigorous supporting expansion; no author endorsement is implied.

items.statement: For a capped adaptive algorithm represented on a common dummy-filled history space, replacing one conditional kernel at a time changes the final output law by at most the ideal-history expectation of that call's conditional total-variation error. Summing adjacent hybrids gives the total capped implementation error; a separate capped-versus-uncapped comparison contributes epsilon_cap exactly once.
assumptions: All capped histories and conditional transitions are measurable and use genuine Markov probability kernels.
The ideal and implemented algorithms share a deterministic call cap and dummy continuation convention.
Each local conditional event discrepancy is bounded by an integrable history-dependent budget under the ideal pre-call history law.
The capped ideal output is compared separately with the uncapped ideal algorithm.

obligations.label: Average an almost-everywhere conditional event bound under the ideal history law
Apply the same downstream Markov continuation after one replaced call
Sum adjacent hybrid event discrepancies over the deterministic cap
Construct measurable dummy-filled histories and identify the paper's delta_t
Compare capped and uncapped ideal outputs and add epsilon_cap once

bindings.boundary: Mean eventwise conditional error only; no history construction, TV-supremum measurability, dummy continuation or cap comparison.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper writes delta_t as expected conditional TV under the ideal history.
assumption_deltas.lean: An explicit integrable real budget epsilon dominates every measurable-event discrepancy almost everywhere under an arbitrary probability input law.
assumption_deltas.reason: The explicit budget and integrability witness make the source averaging step mathematically defined without requiring measurability of a supremum representation of TV.

bindings.boundary: Common Markov suffix only; proving that the paper's later adaptive calls define this suffix is still open.

assumption_deltas.source: The source says subsequent calls are shared by adjacent hybrids.
assumption_deltas.lean: A single explicit Markov kernel S represents all later computation on both sides.
assumption_deltas.reason: Encoding the retained history in the state is necessary for the informal shared-continuation statement to be a valid data-processing application.

bindings.boundary: Finite real triangle telescope only; dummy histories, conditional kernel bounds and epsilon_cap remain separate.

assumption_deltas.source: The source telescopes a finite family of capped hybrid output laws.
assumption_deltas.lean: An arbitrary real sequence with adjacent absolute-difference bounds is telescoped over Finset.range n.
assumption_deltas.reason: The probability-law application is a direct specialization for one measurable output event.
